Updated request scope as of 5/17/24 refinement sent by Mr.Small:

We have put some thought into search restrictions and terms and here is what we would suggest:

(1) total time range of January 1, 2023 through July 31, 2023
(2) Anything that includes Juli Beth Hinds, Dr. Amy Lerner, urban studies and planning (USP), global policy & strategy (GPS), UCSD in conjunction with any of those terms
(3) Anything related to the regional water equity report or RDF
(4) Anything containing a reference to "Juli Beth Hinds, Dr Amy Lerner,  Geosyntec, USP, GPS, or the RWER or RDF", UCSD in conjunction with any of those terms sent to or from "Elise Ruiz, anyone at Murakawa Communications, anyone at Geosyntec including but not limited to Ken Susillo, Megan Otto, Stephanie Zinn; and anyone at the County including but not limited to Stephanie Gaines, Crystal Benham, Todd Snyder, Sarah Agassi, Eden Brukman, and Murtaza Baxamusa"

Original Request:

To Whom it may Concern:
I am writing on behalf of my client Juli Beth Hinds. On behalf of Ms. Hinds, please consider this a formal request pursuant to California Public Records Act, Government Code §6250 et seq. for copies of all DOCUMENTS of the County of San Diego Land Use & Environment Group that reference or relate to: Juli Beth Hinds; the Department of Urban Studies and Planning at the University of California San Diego; or Nathan Fletcher. ("DOCUMENTS" as used herein, shall be defined to mean any ''writing'' as that term is defined in Evidence Code section 250, including, but not limited to, correspondence, emails, texts, communications of any kind, recordings, tapes, computer print-outs, records, slides, photographs, notes, working papers, written analyses, memoranda, plans, telegraphs, telexes and transcriptions, electronic data, and notes or memoranda made by any telephone communications.) This request encompasses all DOCUMENTS dated or created between the dates of January 1, 2022 through the date of this letter.
I request delivery of these records to our firm's office, located at 402 W. Broadway, Suite 1270, San Diego, CA 92101, or we can arrange to pick them up at a reasonable location designated by the County.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Subject: Agenda and Goals for Nov 7 workshop at UCSD

We began the journey on the Regional Decarbonization Framework (RDF) last year in January when our Board of Supervisors directed us to work with UCSD on bringing the best available science to address a challenge that none of us can address in silos on our own – that of decarbonizing every major emitting sector in the region no matter where the emissions originate, for emissions know no boundaries.

As we are now transitioning from study to implementation, we are asking what can we do collectively in partnership with universities, business, labor and community, that will give us greater efficiencies in scale and speed to address climate change in the most effective and humane way possible. All of us from the County have sustainability embedded within the strategic direction of each of our departments. The goals of this workshop are to think about what more can we do? How do we implement sustainability within our core functions? How do we add value to our existing programs so that they also meet the goals of decarbonization? What new programs can achieve a better outcome?

We are meeting offsite at the Public Engagement Building at UCSD to visualize that greener future.

> Report to the Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County (APG)
> On July 16th the first scheduled evacuation tour for SANDAG and Caltrans
> staff was held in the Ramona area. Currently in the planning stages is an
> evacuation tour for the SR 94 area.
>
> APG's representative on the SANDAG Board of Directors, Robin Joy Maxson,
> extended an invitation to SANDAG and Caltrans staff to participate in a
> tour of the expected routes for evacuation in the event of a wildfire or
> other emergency. Maxson emphasised the importance of experiencing the
> evacuation routes in-person in order to accurately evaluate the routes for
> safety and viability in an emergency.
>
> Roadways examined were Wildcat Canyon, SR 67, Highland Valley Road and SR
> 78.
>
> Issues considered and discussed were:
> - Shelter-in-place orders and the likelihood of evacuees choosing to heed
> evacuation orders. Visitors will most likely choose to leave the area.
> - Physical constraints to safe and effective evacuation,  e.g., present
> roadway design, traffic bottlenecks due to changes in the number of lanes
> and/or their configuration.
> - The presence of deadly chimney effect fires and other geographical
> hazards to evacuee safety.
> - Residents and visitors vary in familiarity with the roadways.
> - Fluctuation in the numbers of evacuees on any given day as the number of
> residents is not a static indicator of how many people may need to
> evacuate; the number of weekend visitors to the area greatly expands the
> number of evacuees.
>  - Types of vehicles utilized during an evacuation in rural areas have
> historically been large vehicles/trucks and many vehicle/trailer
> combinations in order to evacuate livestock.
> - The unpredictability of fire during a firestorm created by the combined
> conditions of high temperatures, dry fuel and high winds.
>
> Local fire behavior expert, Dan Summers, identified and explained to the
> group the behavior of fire as it relates to evacuees safety during an
> evacuation event on these four routes. Evacuees are exposed to:
> - Oxygen deprivation which also deprives combustion engine vehicles of the
> oxygen required to operate.
> - Extreme heat which impairs human judgement.
> - Chimney effect fires which are corridors in the landscape where heavy
> brush and trees combine to create a rapid, deadly, blistering, upward burn
> path.
>
> The tour was educational as attendees shared their knowledge of roadway
> construction, fire behavior and human behavior during a crisis.

I’m writing in support of Stoney Oaks Ranch ahead of the community planning group meeting tomorrow.

Stoney Oaks Ranch has been a little slice of heaven for my two girls. Almost 3 years ago, for my oldest’s 5th birthday we reached out about hosting our party there and she has been hooked ever since.

We have attended their once a week camps, summer camps, and take horse riding lessons as well.

My girls have learned skills they wouldn’t have learned had they not had people like Angie and Krystal leading the way to teach kids from a young age a deep appreciation for being outdoors, working with your hands, and caring for animals. Kids don’t just get to show up and play. They work hard and they learn. They learn about respect, and responsibility, how to work as a team, and even self confidence. And when it’s time to go home, they don’t want to leave because they are where children should be: outside, climbing in a treehouse, getting dirty, and exploring.

We live in a small home with a small yard and what my girls get to experience at Stoney Oaks is unique and something they can’t get by just walking into our own backyard. Certainly not the joy and therapeutic wonder of being around horses and other farm animals!

We’re so grateful for everyone at Stoney Oaks Ranch and our weekly schedule has felt empty without my kids being able to gather with other kids who share the same love of being outside and caring for animals.

We LOVE Stoney Oaks and give our full whole hearted support to everything they do.

Sincerely,
Vittoria Allen

Hi Maggie, 

  

I hope you and your family are doing great! 

  

Thank you for your efforts in utilizing  Supervisor Anderson's lakes initiative to reverse the recent threat of further reductions to the access at some of the east county area lakes. Your work has not gone unnoticed. The idea of Supervisor Anderson the COSD becoming involved in rural lakes is always popular.

  

One part of Supervisor Anderson's success with the recent threat of access loss was a petition.

  

Given Supervisor Anderson's many letters of support for Sunrise to Sunset access and other issues at Loveland Reservoir, combined with the inclusion of Sweetwater Authority lakes named in Supervisor Anderson's initiative and work by Brian Albright's Parks and Recreation,  I am hoping that Supervisor Anderson would consider spearheading a petition to open Loveland Reservoir from Sunrise to Sunset. I understand there is a possibility of the petition failing in the short term, which is undesirable. Still, it could get us out of the hopeless situation we are currently in regarding legal and practical access at the Loveland Reservoir for working people.

  

You may know that the non-profit, Friends of Loveland Reservoir's,  compromise to have volunteers close the gates at Sunset failed. Please consider a powerful petition for Sunrise to Sunset according to the easement as the credible land-use policy and next possible productive step.

I have been sharing what has been happening with the Lakes initiative since we met almost four years ago with these leading individuals and groups.  I believe this is a potential case of " a rising tide lifts all boats," which fits Supervisor Anderson's goals and recognition for his district's values and effort for outdoor enthusiasts.
